import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
import io

# Dataset provided as a string
csv_data = """Person ID,Gender,Age,Occupation,Sleep Duration,Quality of Sleep,Physical Activity Level,Stress Level,BMI Category,Blood Pressure,Heart Rate,Daily Steps,Sleep Disorder
1,Male,27,Software Engineer,6.1,6,42,6,Overweight,126/83,77,4200,
2,Male,28,Doctor,6.2,6,60,8,Normal,125/80,75,10000,
3,Male,28,Doctor,6.2,6,60,8,Normal,125/80,75,10000,
4,Male,28,Sales Representative,5.9,4,30,8,Obese,140/90,85,3000,Sleep Apnea
5,Male,28,Sales Representative,5.9,4,30,8,Obese,140/90,85,3000,Sleep Apnea
"""

# Read the dataset into a pandas DataFrame
df = pd.read_csv(io.StringIO(csv_data))

# Set a clean style for the plots
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid")

# Create a figure with two subplots
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(16, 6))

# --- Plot 1: Scatter plot of Sleep Duration vs. Quality of Sleep, colored by Stress Level ---
# This plot explores the direct relationship between sleep duration and quality,
# and how stress level might influence it. Age is used to vary marker size.
sns.scatterplot(
    data=df,
    x='Sleep Duration',
    y='Quality of Sleep',
    hue='Stress Level',
    size='Age',
    sizes=(80, 400), # Define a range for marker sizes
    palette='viridis', # A perceptually uniform colormap
    ax=axes[0],
    alpha=0.8,
    legend='full'
)
axes[0].set_title('Sleep Duration vs. Quality of Sleep by Stress & Age', fontsize=14)
axes[0].set_xlabel('Sleep Duration (hours)', fontsize=12)
axes[0].set_ylabel('Quality of Sleep (1-10)', fontsize=12)
axes[0].grid(True, linestyle='--', alpha=0.6)
axes[0].tick_params(labelsize=10)


# --- Plot 2: Strip plot combined with a transparent box plot for Sleep Duration by BMI Category ---
# This plot shows the distribution of sleep duration across different BMI categories.
# A stripplot is used to show individual data points, which is especially useful for small datasets.
# A transparent boxplot is overlaid to indicate median and range.
bmi_order = ['Normal', 'Overweight', 'Obese']
df['BMI Category'] = pd.Categorical(df['BMI Category'], categories=bmi_order, ordered=True)

sns.stripplot(
    data=df,
    x='BMI Category',
    y='Sleep Duration',
    hue='Gender', # Use Gender as hue to differentiate points
    jitter=0.15, # Add jitter to prevent points from overlapping
    palette='coolwarm',
    ax=axes[1],
    size=9, # Adjust point size for better visibility
    edgecolor='gray', # Add edge color for better distinction
    linewidth=0.8,
    legend='full'
)
# Overlay a transparent boxplot to show central tendency and spread
sns.boxplot(
    data=df,
    x='BMI Category',
    y='Sleep Duration',
    ax=axes[1],
    color='white', # Set boxplot color to white
    boxprops={'alpha': 0.3}, # Make boxplot transparent
    whiskerprops={'alpha': 0.3},
    medianprops={'color': 'black', 'linewidth': 2},
    capprops={'alpha': 0.3},
    showfliers=False # Do not show outliers, as stripplot already shows all points
)
axes[1].set_title('Sleep Duration Distribution by BMI Category & Gender', fontsize=14)
axes[1].set_xlabel('BMI Category', fontsize=12)
axes[1].set_ylabel('Sleep Duration (hours)', fontsize=12)
axes[1].grid(True, linestyle='--', alpha=0.6)
axes[1].tick_params(labelsize=10)
# Adjust legend position to avoid overlap
axes[1].legend(title='Gender', loc='upper right', bbox_to_anchor=(1, 1))


# Add a main title for the entire figure
plt.suptitle('Key Relationships in Sleep and Health Metrics', fontsize=16, y=1.02)

# Adjust layout to prevent titles/labels from overlapping
plt.tight_layout(rect=[0, 0.03, 1, 0.95])

# Save the plot as a PNG file with high resolution
plt.savefig('output.png', dpi=300)
